question: Who are our 3 weakest players? (least valuable to keep for the rest of the season in GONG scoring; the first three we would drop)
taken: # Players already off the board, one per line. Lines starting with # are ignored.
# Full draft: see council/draft_results.csv for all 104 picks.
method: Each member ranks all 13 active players weakest-first. Three sequential selection counts by tally.py: weakest #1 over all 13; #2 and #3 with earlier picks removed. A member's vote in each count is their highest-ranked remaining player; runoffs are derived from the same full rankings. Jimmy Butler III (IR, out until at least 2 Jan) is not a candidate.

ballots.rationale: With 3 bench spots, about 7 adds a week and daily lineups, a roster spot is worth its per-game margin over the ~32-34 FP/G waiver level (Queta 33.40/76 GP, Nembhard 35.17, McCollum 32.68). Ware is at that level: 32.47 over 77 GP on 22.2 min, projected ~34.5, behind Turner, and Sims started over him on 14 Oct. Wilson has zero NBA games, a 34.88 projection and a 22.4 FP/G preseason with 17 TO in 5 games. Rollins' 37.51 actual is marked down to ~32.8 by ESPN and to 30-33 by the offseason doc now that Herro is in. George (36 years old, 55 projected GP) is fourth, roughly level with Rollins once the games he misses are streamed.

ballots.rationale: Dejounte Murray has the worst availability profile: 14 games last season (THIN), 45 games over two Pelicans seasons, a toe contusion that cost him the last three exhibitions and has him questionable for the opener, and Fears pushing for his role. About 37 FP/g over about 50 games is roughly 1,850 points against roughly 2,415 from a free agent at 34.5 x 70. George ranks second on the same maths: age 36, 37 GP last season, P_GP 55, roughly 36 x 52 = about 1,870, but he is healthy for the opener. Ware is third: 77 GP but 32.47 FP/g in 22.2 minutes is below the healthy free agents (Nembhard 35.17, Holiday 34.93, Queta 33.40), and he came off the bench behind Turner and even Sims.

His preseason scores 22.4 FP/g in 26.6 mpg (30-69 FG, 17 TO in 5 games), and even ESPN's 34.88 projection is barely above the 32-34 FP/g that waiver players give (Wiggins 33.78, Queta 33.40, McCollum 32.68). That puts his season total (about 2,000-2,160) below Dejounte Murray's projection (39.05+0.50 over 68 GP), even though Murray's role is in doubt.
